newsitem.title: VIETNAM: Vietnam army rebuked over lavishness, corruption.
newsitem.headline: Vietnam army rebuked over lavishness, corruption.

text.p: Vietnam's military, one of the region's largest, was warned on Wednesday that it needed to do more to stamp out wastefulness and corruption while improving its financial management.

The official Quan Doi Nhan Dan (People's Army) newspaper said in a commentary that some army units were registering "big losses" as a result of casual spending on parties, ceremonies and hosting guests.
It said weak financial management of army construction projects was also contributing to losses.
"There are loopholes which have led to corruption among some army units and army officials," it said, adding that the army should take measures to increase revenue.
Vietnam's estimated 572,000-strong military has enjoyed the fruits of the country's economic reform process and a number of units own factories, farms or other commercial enterprises.
